title: Atomic Security Concerns: Towards a Foundational Language for Security Knowledge Representation
abstract: arXiv:2610.35782v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Cybersecurity governance, risk management, compliance, and security architecture rely on numerous concepts, including security properties, domains, controls, risks, implementation measures, capabilities, and compliance requirements. Although these concepts are widely used, they are often represented through heterogeneous abstractions and vocabularies, making relationships among them difficult to express consistently and leaving much of the associated reasoning dependent on expert knowledge. translated_title: 原子安全关注点：迈向安全知识表示的基础语言
translated_abstract: 网络安全治理、风险管理、合规性以及安全架构依赖于众多概念，包括安全属性、领域、控制措施、风险、实施措施、能力和合规要求。尽管这些概念被广泛使用，但它们通常通过异构的抽象和词汇来表示，使得它们之间的关系难以一致地表达，并且大量相关推理依赖于专家知识。本文引入了“安全关注点”和“原子安全关注点”的概念，并探讨了一个假设：网络安全知识可以通过一组有限的基础关注点来表示。受化学中原子角色的启发，所提出的方法将网络安全概念视为更基础关注点的组合，而非独立的抽象。因此，原子安全关注点可以被视为一种通……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文受化学原子概念启发，提出“原子安全关注点”的概念，并假设网络安全知识可以通过一组有限的基础关注点的组合来表示，从而为安全知识表示奠定一种基础语言。
en_tdlr: Inspired by the role of atoms in chemistry, this paper introduces Atomic Security Concerns (ASCs) and hypothesizes that cybersecurity knowledge can be represented as compositions of a finite set of foundational concerns, providing a foundational language for security knowledge representation.
